**Selected recipe: 0.2 Torr chamber pressure with a −5 °C shelf.** Predicted complete drying at **17.79 h** (last solver node, 100% dried). A feasible recipe exists, so no_feasible_recipe does not apply.

**Constraint margins for this pair** (native solver outputs; whole-batch figures derived from them):
- **Vial-bottom temperature:** maximum returned value −18.70 °C vs the −18.0 °C critical limit → **0.70 °C of headroom**. That maximum falls at the final node (17.79 h), exactly when drying completes.
- **Whole-batch equipment line:** peak returned flux 0.63123 kg/h/m² × 0.124972 m² total product area (3.14 cm² × 398 vials) = 0.0789 kg/h whole batch, against the line −0.182 + 11.7 × 0.2 = 2.158 kg/h → **2.079 kg/h headroom** (~3.7% of the line used).

**Why faster pairs lose:** the three 10 °C shelf recipes dry fastest (10.97–13.02 h) but their maximum returned vial-bottom temperatures are −13.84 to −17.07 °C, above the −18.0 °C limit. The 0.2 Torr / −25 °C pair never completes within the 60 h horizon (88.25% dried at 60 h). The equipment line never binds for any of the 12 candidates — temperature is the binding constraint. Next-fastest feasible pairs are 0.1 Torr / −5 °C (18.85 h) and 0.05 Torr / −5 °C (19.67 h).

**What I could not check or do:**
- **The save did not run.** The budget was reached before lyopronto_record_result could be called, so this assessment is not recorded anywhere, and the native simulation results were not written into a saved record.
- **Between-node excursions:** the constraint holds on returned solver nodes only — the simulator gives no continuous-maximum guarantee. With only 0.70 °C of headroom, a rerun with a smaller time step is the check that would settle whether the vial bottom stays at or below −18.0 °C between nodes; I could not run it.

This is a synthetic, authored simulator-world case with no experimental measurements: the times and temperatures above are model predictions from the native LyoPRONTO run, not a measured outcome, and nothing here operates equipment or approves a recipe for production.
